decision.title: HTML5 parsing: a hand-written tokenizer, tree construction on a working tree (packet 7.10a)
decision.summary: fn:parse-html and fn:html-doc are the optional feature "html": a hand-written HTML tokenizer and tree construction on an , not tree-sitter, then mapped to XDM.

body.p: , after , , , , , , , . fn:parse-html and fn:html-doc (F&O 4.0, 17.3) as the optional feature sxml_html_parser_feature() (name "html"), after the HTML Living Standard of 16 October 2026, 13.2.

item.p: Not tree-sitter (an exception to , for the reasons of ): (1) the tokenizer is a state machine that tree construction switches (RCDATA, RAWTEXT, script data and PLAINTEXT after a start tag, CDATA sections only when the adjusted current node is foreign), so lexing depends on parse state a context-free grammar does not see; (2) HTML has no syntax errors: every input parses, by error recovery the standard defines exactly, whereas makes any ERROR node a static error and tree-sitter's own recovery is not the standard's; (3) tree construction moves nodes already built (adoption agency, foster parenting), so a walk over a concrete syntax tree would be a second tree builder, not a replacement for one; (4) the input is run-time data (parse-html($computed)), and tree-sitter allocates with malloc outside every allocator and limit, which accepts only for source text.

Files: src/html_tokenizer.c (the 84 states of 13.2.5 as one loop over a state variable; tree construction pulls tokens, characters come in runs); src/html_tree_construction.c (the 21 insertion modes and the rules for foreign content as a dispatch loop of steps, so "process the token using the rules for" is no call cycle, ); src/html.c (the walk that sends the working tree to an arena tree, the XDM mapping, the feature); src/html_encoding.c and the generated src/html_encoding_tables.c (tools/generate-html-encodings.py); src/function_library_html.c (the two rows, 's library functions, not a registered part); src/html_internal.h.

Working tree (glossary ): node, attribute and text-segment tables in allocator memory; a text node is a chain of segments so that later characters join it; the walk to the tree builder follows parent links (no stack needed). The named character references are fn:char's table (src/unicode_tables.c) plus the 106 names that also match without ";": no second entity table.

The standard as of now: processing instructions (13.2.5.72 to .76: <?target data?> is a PI, <?xml ...?> a comment), no "in select" insertion modes, search special, select a scope boundary. F&O 4.0's note that the HTML parser makes no PIs predates that change.

Not done, by the standard's own switches: scripting is Disabled (noscript content is parsed; 13.2.4.5), no fragment case, no declarative shadow roots, no sanitizer, no content patching (template for); selectedcontent is filled by DOM steps of the select element, not by the parser, so it stays empty.

XDM mapping (F&O 4.0, 17.3.1; HTML, 13.2.9): XHTML, SVG and MathML namespaces; SVG and MathML names in their case; xlink: and xml: attributes in their namespaces; xmlns attributes dropped; names XML does not allow escaped as "U" and six hex digits; comments get a space inside "--" and after a final "-"; U+000C becomes a space and other characters XML does not allow U+FFFD; an id that is an NCName is an ID; a template's contents are its children. Base URI: the static base URI (fn:parse-html), the resource's URI (fn:html-doc, also its document URI).

Input (13.2.3): a string is UTF-8 with a known encoding, a leading U+FEFF stripped (F&O 4.0); octets: byte order mark, then the encoding option (every label of the Encoding Standard; its 28 single-byte encodings, UTF-8, UTF-16 and x-user-defined decode, a multi-byte or unknown label is FODC0011), then step 9's autodetection: well-formed UTF-8, else windows-1252 (step 10). No <meta> prescan yet (7.10b).
fail-on-error: parsing stops at the first parse error (13.2.2 allows it), a decoding error included: FODC0011. Unknown options and html-version, method or include-template-content are XPTY0004.

Counts (release driver): fn-parse-html 0 to 22 of 22 (XQ40 and XP40), fn-html-doc 0 to 9 of 10 (html-doc-010 expects FODC0011 for <a:tag>, which no rule of 13.2 makes a parse error), misc-HtmlTestSuite 0 to 1,378 of 1,379 (XQ40; html-test-1281 expects jsoup's comment for <?processing data?>), misc-BuiltInKeywords +2 (the result type document-node(*:html)?). The sets are no non-goals of the QT4 driver any more. Outside the suite, the html5lib tests of web-platform-tests run in a scratch harness: tree construction 1,747 of 1,753 (#script-on and fragment cases left out; the others are selectedcontent and harness limits), tokenizer 7,022 of 7,049 (the rest harness limits and F&O's U+FEFF rule).

Sizes (stripped / gzipped): sxml.wasm 2,078,210 / 722,803 before and after (no HTML code links into the core); sxml-full.wasm 2,103,528 / 733,247 to 2,182,635 / 762,413 (+79,107; budget 3,000,000); the sxml CLI module 5,848,173 / 1,239,159 to 5,927,297 / 1,267,818. The CLI module was over its 5,500,000-byte budget already (Proposed below).

Tested: tests/html_test.c (tokens, trees, the input stream, both functions with and without the feature, allocation-failure loops), tests/fuzz/html_parse_fuzz.c (11,000 runs seeded from the suite, no finding), two sxml xpath end-to-end tests.

Left for 7.10b: the <meta> prescan of 13.2.3.2 (step 5) and 13.2.3.4 (changing the encoding while parsing) for octets; vendoring the html5lib .dat and tokenizer tests (web-platform-tests html/syntax/parsing/resources, html5lib-tests tokenizer) as a unit test with the scratch harness's format; the multi-byte decoders (Shift_JIS, EUC-JP, ISO-2022-JP, GBK, gb18030, Big5, EUC-KR) or a decision that they stay FODC0011; source locations for dm:location; XHTML (the XML syntax) recognition, which F&O 4.0 asks for with "should"; the CLI's relative URIs in sxml xpath and sxml xquery (no static base URI, so fn:html-doc and fn:unparsed-text of a relative name fail there); html-doc-010 and html-test-1281 stay failing unless the suite changes.
